chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'A Penalty (Hadd) would not be established upon anyone in the land of the enemy'.

key_terms.أَرْضُ الْعَدُوِّ: Land of the enemy / Enemy territory
key_terms.حَدٌّ: Fixed Islamic penalty for a specific crime

ai.seo_question: When is a Hadd penalty not applied according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Yunus ibn Ya'qub, establishes that fixed penalties (Hudud) are not executed in enemy territory (Ard al--'Adw), reflecting the Shia juristic view that the conditions for Hadd enforcement, such as security and full judicial authority, are often compromised abroad. This ruling underscores the principle that Hudud are subject to specific contextual prerequisites and are not automatically applicable in all geographical locations, a nuance emphasized by scholars like Al-Kulayni in organizing this chapter on the timings and conditions of penalty application.
